issues.body: `evaluate()` expands every context but de-duplicates solely on the expanded `dedup_key`. Therefore a template such as `dedup_key = "follow-up-{pr}"`, `title = "Follow up {crate}"` produces only the first crate's issue, despite the new documented contract that a template naming `{crate}` is minted once per added crate. The new crate-agnostic test contains no `{crate}` in any field, while the per-crate test also puts `{crate}` in the key, so neither exposes this acceptance gap. This is silent incomplete fan-out and makes the behavior depend on an undocumented coupling between presentation fields and identity.
issues.fix_hint: Define and enforce a coherent identity rule. Prefer detecting whether any template field contains `{crate}` and ensuring its effective dedup key is per-crate (for example by incorporating the crate into the key), or reject templates that use `{crate}` outside the key without including it in `dedup_key`. Add a regression test with `{crate}` in title/body but not the configured key and update the TOML documentation to match the chosen contract.
issues.title: Per-crate templates are dropped when the dedup key is crate-agnostic

verdict.summary: The fan-out works only when `{crate}` changes the dedup key, but the documented contract says any template naming `{crate}` is emitted once per added crate. A template that uses `{crate}` only in its title or body is silently collapsed to the first crate by `seen_keys`, so the implementation and tests do not cover the full promised behavior.
